parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Restoring-acceleration scale; torque divided by unknown inertia.

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: Positive linear viscous damping rate, including effective motor back EMF.

parameters.name: cp
parameters.description: Positive-direction dry-friction acceleration capacity; symmetric capacity when no negative-direction parameter is present.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Positive voltage-to-acceleration gain, or zero-voltage slope when motor saturation is present.

parameters.name: tau
parameters.description: Velocity-relaxation time in the static-friction projection; a numerical/constitutive regularization, not an identified electrical time constant.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Nonnegative motor saturation curvature; empirical decrease of incremental voltage gain with voltage magnitude.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: Relative cosine modulation of sinusoidal restoring acceleration; represents a second angular harmonic, without assigning a specific mechanical source.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared open-loop angle errors `theta_sim-theta` (rad), pooled over all samples except the first in each trajectory, with equal weight per sample. This directly matches the intended long-horizon angle criterion and avoids treating centrally differenced acceleration as an exact torque measurement. Each run starts from its logged initial angle and angular velocity; input voltage is held constant for each integration interval of `T_s = 0.01` s, as specified in TASK.md.
estimation.data: Final coefficient fit: all trajectories and rows of `data/train.csv` and `data/val.csv`, with first rows used only as initial states. Validation data were deliberately included after preliminary train-only comparisons because there are few independent driven records. No test data were accessed. Separate train-only validation and leave-one-trajectory-out analyses are recorded in `refine_results.json`; all within-trajectory ordering is preserved.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares by the trust-region reflective method, `scipy.optimize.least_squares`, with classical RK4 simulation implemented in NumPy/Numba. Every fitted parameter in this candidate was estimated jointly in the final supplied-data fit, with no parameter transferred as fixed from another candidate. Starting values were `g = 108` rad/s^2, `b = 1.6` 1/s, `cp = 18` rad/s^2, `k = 26.5` rad/(s^2 V), `tau = 0.02` s, `m = 0.05` 1/V, `a = 0.03`, `cn = 21` rad/s^2. The first four starts were rounded pilot moving-row derivative estimates; the regularization and extension starts were deliberately moderate physically admissible guesses. Bounds were `70 <= g <= 150` rad/s^2, `0.05 <= b <= 6` 1/s, `5 <= cp <= 40` rad/s^2, `15 <= k <= 60` rad/(s^2 V), `0.004 <= tau <= 0.12` s, `0 <= m <= 0.4` 1/V, `-0.5 <= a <= 0.5`, `5 <= cn <= 40` rad/s^2. Positive dissipation/gain and bounded modulation enforce physical sign constraints; the relaxation lower bound limits stiffness at the prescribed integration step. For the compensated model the speed-width lower bound limits stiffness instead. The upper bounds prevent poorly identified extreme regimes, not claimed hardware limits. Jacobian-based variable scaling and relative finite-difference step `diff_step = 0.0001` were used; stopping tolerances were `ftol = 1e-9`, `xtol = 1e-9`, `gtol = 1e-7`, with at most `max_nfev = 400` function evaluations per fit. These optimizer settings are dimensionless. No random numbers were used in estimation. A train-only fit and leave-one-trajectory-out fits were separate diagnostics and did not supply fixed coefficients to the final candidate. Cross-validation fits started from this candidate's full-data optimum, excluding the held trajectory from the objective; these are not independently initialized, untouched validation tests.

discussion.family: Continuous clipped-force static/Coulomb-friction model with velocity relaxation, harmonic restoring torque, asymmetric friction, and a monotone saturating motor characteristic. Physical dry-friction modeling follows the Coulomb/viscous and static-friction distinctions in B. Armstrong-Helouvry, Control of Machines with Friction (1991), cited from memory, not source-checked. The algebraic regularizations below are proposed approximations, not the exact algorithm of that reference.
discussion.interpretation: `theta` is angle (rad), `omega` is angular velocity (rad/s), `u` is motor voltage (V), `dtheta` and `domega` are their time derivatives (rad/s and rad/s^2). Every constant is defined in the parameter rows. The unprojected acceleration is `k*u/(1+m*Abs(u))-g*sin(theta)*(1+a*cos(theta))-b*omega`. Its voltage term drives the motor; its sine term is restoring; its linear velocity term is dissipative. `-g*sin(theta)*(1+a*cos(theta))` adds a constrained second angular harmonic; `a` has an empirical mathematical role, not a uniquely determined mechanical cause. `k*u/(1+m*Abs(u))` is an empirical saturating motor map with positive incremental gain. Subtracting `Min(cp,Max(-cn,k*u/(1+m*Abs(u))-g*sin(theta)*(1+a*cos(theta))-b*omega+omega/tau))` gives bounded dry-friction acceleration. While the clip is inactive, the resulting law is `-omega/tau`; at rest it exactly cancels admissible net force. During sufficiently fast motion the clipped term reaches its appropriate friction capacity.
discussion.origin: The sinusoidal restoring term, linear motor gain, viscous damping, and bounded opposing dry-friction force came from physical reasoning. Pilot constrained linear derivative regressions in `helper_analysis.py` on moving training rows supported this starting structure. The static projection was proposed to cover the many resting samples, rather than applying `sign(omega)` at rest. Moving derivative residuals showed modest directional bias and angle dependence. The unequal directional capacities and second restoring harmonic address those patterns. A positive quadratic voltage extension collapsed to its zero-curvature bound in training simulation fitting, so I tested the opposite, monotone saturating response `k*u/(1+m*Abs(u))`. Its positive fitted curvature improved supplied-data trajectory cross-validation slightly; this is empirical saturation, not proof of a motor-circuit mechanism. No unrestricted symbolic-regression search was used: compact constrained force-balance families allowed exact sign arguments, and the derivative diagnostics did not justify a high-complexity search.
discussion.limitations: Only effective torque/inertia ratios are identifiable; inertia, motor resistance, contact forces, and separate bearing/motor losses are unknown. Encoder quantization and numerical differentiation contaminate the derivative target. Actual training voltage spans approximately `-4.9451 <= u <= 3.9525` V; the required larger voltage domain is extrapolation. The low-speed transition is poorly identified, and is partly a numerical regularization for the specified RK4 step `T_s = 0.01` s from TASK.md. No hysteresis, electrical state, friction aging, or trajectory-specific calibration is represented. Some residual free-response endpoint differences remain; I did not add per-trajectory offsets because there must be one autonomous state law. At zero speed and zero voltage the unprojected force is restoring; clipping it to an interval containing zero preserves that sign or cancels it, establishing R2. The restoring factor remains positive by the fitted constraints. For fixed states the derivative of the clipped-force subtraction with respect to unprojected force is either zero or one, so composition with the monotone motor map establishes R3. `dtheta = omega` enforces R1 identically. Supplied-data cross-validation RMSE was `0.072298` rad; final-fit pooled RMSE was `0.061758` rad, both computed on angle samples after each trajectory's first sample. The train-only fit scored `0.093983` rad on `data/val.csv`, before this final refit. Model structures were compared using the supplied data, so cross-validation is selection evidence, not an unbiased hidden-test estimate. Dense physical grids and stress runs in `diagnostics.py` supplement the sign arguments but do not prove global simulation accuracy.
